title: En el mercado
blurbEn: Saturday at the market with Ana's grandmother, and the words for buying things by weight.
body:
Los sábados por la mañana voy al mercado con mi abuela.

En el mercado hay muchas frutas y verduras. Todo es más barato que en el supermercado, y mi abuela dice que también es mejor.

—¿Puedo probar una naranja? —pregunta mi abuela.

—Claro, señora.

Compramos un kilo de naranjas, medio kilo de tomates y una docena de huevos.

Volvemos a casa despacio, con mucha comida y poco dinero.
translationEn:
On Saturday mornings I go to the market with my grandmother.

At the market there is a lot of fruit and vegetables. Everything is cheaper than at the supermarket, and my grandmother says it is better too.

"Can I try an orange?" my grandmother asks.

"Of course, madam."

We buy a kilo of oranges, half a kilo of tomatoes and a dozen eggs.

We go home slowly, with a lot of food and little money.

medio.note: The same word as in 'las tres y media'. Here it counts weight rather than time.

phrases.note: 'más ... que' is how Spanish compares two things.
'poder' + a plain verb. The second verb never changes.
